root_idea.summary: The root denotes the state opposite cold: warmth or heat.
root_idea.development: The semantic field extends from warmth itself to clothing, shelter, and useful livestock products that provide warmth or benefit, with further conventional extensions to seasonal phenomena, abundance, and bodily curvature.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Quranic noun دِفْء.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the word denotes warmth associated with livestock and their use, especially protection from cold.

senses.definition: The useful products and benefits obtained from livestock, including offspring, hair or fur, milk, and related produce.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an explicitly reported interpretation of the occurrence in 16:5; the connection with warmth is the use of livestock hair and wool for warm clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become warm or hot; to experience warmth or heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is also used of dwellings, garments, days, and nights that are warm or hot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wear clothing or another covering that makes one warm; to warm oneself with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe protection from cold or the use of a garment as a source of warmth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To warm oneself or put on what makes one warm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These related derived forms are used of seeking or obtaining warmth through clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone warm or hot; to clothe someone in a garment that provides warmth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person, and the warming garment is described as woolen or similar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone a large or abundant gift; to give much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a tropical or extended usage of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a group of people to gather together, apparently so that they warm one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective action is understood through the mutual production of warmth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to exceed one hundred in number.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized Classical usage applied to a camel herd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a Yemeni dialect, to dispatch a wounded person, that is, to put him to death quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is explicitly dialectal and applies to a wounded person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment, covering, or other thing that renders a person warm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited materials include wool, camel hair, and similar substances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shelter that protects from cold wind and provides warmth, such as the lee of a wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote a warm sheltered place rather than a garment or material.
This is reported as an assumed tropical extension distinct from the ordinary sense of warmth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A forward bending or curvature of the upper back over the breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is an anatomical or bodily description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Warmly clad; also warm or hot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied in the cited usages to people, garments, places, and times, with corresponding feminine and plural forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain associated with the seasonal transition after heat has strengthened, around the period after spring and before or at the beginning of summer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Authorities differ in the precise seasonal boundaries of the term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Provision or grain brought in the early part of the warm season or summer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is used substantivally for a seasonal supply of provisions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The offspring of sheep or goats born at the end of winter or during the associated seasonal period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some authorities extend the term to offspring produced at any time.
The corresponding feminine form is also reported; spelling varies in some transmitted copies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels abundant in fur and fat, and thus warm through their covering; related forms may also denote a numerous herd whose members warm one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description is applied to camels and is explained either by their own fur and fat or by the warmth generated when many are together.

cautions: The single Quranic occurrence at 16:5 supports both the ordinary sense “warmth” and an explicitly reported interpretation referring to useful livestock products; the evidence does not require choosing only one of these readings.
The seasonal term دَفَئِيّ has differing reported boundaries, and the offspring usage is likewise attributed with differing scope.
